newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks down after Jospin speech.
newsitem.headline: French stocks down after Jospin speech.

text.p: France's blue-chip CAC-40 share index lost 60 points in little over an hour as market sentiment slumped on Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's keynote policy address to parliament, but the market came off its lows.
"People are starting to catch on to what's going on," a broker said, referring to the bourse's advance since the Socialists' victory on June 1 on expectations of moderation.
Shares in companies involved in privatisations and restructurings fell, while retail shares rose against the trend.
The CAC was down 19.25 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,732.49 at 1430 GMT after ranging between 2,790.19 and 2,721.41.
The CAC-40 June futures contract was down 14 at 2,734.

* State-controlled defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF fell more than four percent after Jospin said the government did not favour privatisations but then rose when he said defence companies needed to restructure. The stock was down 0.92 percent at 150.50 francs, while Lagardere, tipped to win the Thomson bidding, fell 1.07 percent to 166.70 francs.
* Alcatel Alsthom was down 1.07 percent, erasing its strong gains on Chairman Serge Tchuruk's forecast that operating profit would more than double this year.
* Restructuring stocks were weaker, notably in the auto sector.
* Retail shares, expected to benefit from a higher minimum wage and less job insecurity, rose. Carrefour was up 0.22 percent, Pinault-Printemps rose 1.4 percent.

* LVMH fell 2.46 percent. Brokers said investors are not happy that chairman Bernard Arnault is buying stock in Grand Met as part of his bid to foil the planned Grand Met-Guinness merger. "People don't like that cavalier attitude," a broker said. "If he's going to pursue them with legal means, fine, but now he's buying stock."
